Vlad sits down with Lil Jungle Boy for a detailed account of an Oakland run that he says turned into an abduction inside an old house basement. He describes being lured during a major drug deal, waking up tied to a chair, and enduring hours of violence as captors demanded information about a stash spot. Lil Jungle Boy also explains how a GPS hidden in his Timberland boot allegedly helped his father and uncle track him from Los Angeles, naming Reggie Wright Sr. while discussing family ties, county jail incidents, and past legal trouble.  

In the interview, he recounts a gunshot wound to the back of his head, emergency treatment near the Bay Area, a coma, a 5150 evaluation, lasting nerve damage, and how the experience shaped his views on gang life, loyalty, snitching, and younger artists pursuing music.

--------
Vlad sits down with comedian TK Kirkland for a sharp conversation on investing, Robinhood, and how everyday people can enter the stock market with small amounts. After discussing Vlad Tenev, the Robinhood CEO reportedly worth billions, they break down fractional shares, Stash, and why more Black and Latino investors are using trading apps. Vlad explains how a loan management account, or stock-backed loan, can let investors borrow against holdings in companies like Amazon, Microsoft, or Nvidia without selling shares—sharing that he partially used this strategy to buy a house. TK adds his perspective on long-term discipline, leaving investments alone, AI-related stocks, Elon Musk-level wealth, and why owning shares in major tech companies can be more powerful than watching from the sidelines. A practical, candid exchange on money, risk, and building wealth through the stock market.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Carlos Lehder details his journey from Armenia, Colombia, to New York, prison in Danbury, and the cocaine routes that helped define the Medellín Cartel era. Lehder discusses meeting Jorge “Boston George” Jung, building the Norman’s Cay operation in the Bahamas, working with Pablo Escobar, and why he says the “cartel” was never a single unified organization. He also addresses the M-19 kidnapping attempt, MAS, Colombian politics, Rodrigo Lara Bonilla, Luis Carlos Galán, his 1987 extradition, and the U.S. case that led to life plus 135 years.

Lehder reflects on cooperating in the Manuel Noriega trial, witness protection, 33 years in federal prison, release in 2020, life in Germany and Colombia, and portrayals in Blow and Netflix’s Narcos. He also shares his warning on drug trafficking, comparing past narco empires with El Chapo and today’s law enforcement technology.
